liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Jam** (5 reviews): Jam grows from nothing on an unfamiliar theme into a frenzy, then dissolves into Wharf Rat; Space into jam into Wharf Rat is the highlight; the two-chord jam leads into Wharf Rat [16][17][20][22][25]
- **Bird Song** (1 review): Bird Song singled out as especially noteworthy [16]
- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodleoo** (1 review): A cut near 5:53 drops Garcia's solo vocal line about the Rio Grande and the lazy river refrain [15]

## Setlist highlights

- **Merry-Go-Round Broke Down," chatter**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **Phil chatter**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **am**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]
- **Jerry Garcia/Bill Graham/Sam Cutler chatter**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1973-07-27.aud.pantagruel.28882.sbeok.flac16** (recommended): audience recording; 14 songs; 96 min; rated 4.5/5 by 2 [1]
- **gd1973-07-27.mtx.seamons.100410.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 12 songs; 101 min; rated 4.86/5 by 7 [2]
- **gd1973-07-27.aud.sirmick.87464.flac16**: audience recording; 13 songs; 98 min; rated 5/5 by 2 [3]
- **gd73-07-27.aud.weiner.gdadt26.26363.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 12 songs; 91 min; rated 4.8/5 by 10 [4]. Said about its sound: Audience recording sounds full with crowd reaction, and lacks the harsh soundboard cuts in Bird Song, Half-Step and the big jam [23]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.weiner.180.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 90 min; rated 4.64/5 by 22 [9]. Said about its sound: Soundboard rated roughly 3.5 to 4 stars with a good mix, but contains cuts and omissions; Soundboard quality is average, with a few cuts [15][16]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.miller.27779.sbeok.flacf**: soundboard; 11 songs; 89 min; rated 4.73/5 by 11 [10]. Said about its sound: This Miller soundboard is a nice upgrade over earlier circulating versions of the soundcheck; Sounds much better than earlier sources, though the same cut in Half-Step remains [19][20]

## Around the show

- Phil told the audience the afternoon performance was a test, suggesting a soundcheck [15]
- Recording was made amid crowded, muddy conditions [23]
- Such out-of-nowhere transitions are rare; similar ones came on 6/14/68, 12/31/71 and 3/27/88 [17]
- The lengthy Bird Song falls short of the one on 8/27/72, but comes close [17]
- The jam's beginning reminded the reviewer of pieces of Mountain Jam [22]
- Reviewer finds this audience source sounds much better than the other circulating audience version used for patches [23]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1973-07-27.aud.pantagruel.28882.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Unknown; transferred by Pantagruel; source: cassette (unknown gen) > HD [1]. Also: Same recording as the principal source of Audience Devotional Tree Round 26, October 2004; Uploader's old cassette seems one generation earlier than the Round 26 principal source, and includes all of Sugaree [1]
- **gd1973-07-27.mtx.seamons.100410.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Hunter Seamons; source: Matrix mix (SBD/AUD) [2]. Also: Soundboard to master reel to 48k DAT, transferred and edited by Charlie Miller; First set was labeled master reel but obviously isn't; audience cassette portions were transferred by Noah Weiner in October 2004 [2]
- **gd1973-07-27.aud.sirmick.87464.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: aud (unknown gen) > ??? > wav > flac [3]. Also: Audience recording had DC offset removed, pitch correction, dropout repairs, and patches from other shnids, then remastered with iZotope Ozone and Waves Z-Noise [3]
- **gd73-07-27.aud.weiner.gdadt26.26363.sbeok.shnf**: source: Audience Recording [4]. Also: Audience cassette from an unknown taper, transferred analog to digital by Noah Weiner via Nakamichi MR-1 and Fostex D5 DAT [4]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.weiner.180.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [9]. Also: This soundboard's text file doesn't document its history; Noah's source apparently differed and lacked some songs [14]
- **gd73-07-27.sbd.miller.27779.sbeok.flacf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [10]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grand Prix Racecourse - July 28, 1973](https://www.dead.net/show/july-28-1973) [27]
